summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and obesity was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure following dietary indiscretion with high sodium intake and noncompliance with evening diuretic therapy. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, significant lower extremity edema, and fluid overload. He was diuresed with IV furosemide, achieving nearly 15 liters of urine output. Due to persistent tachycardia and suboptimal rate control on metoprolol, he underwent transesophageal echocardiography which showed no intracardiac thrombus, followed by successful DC cardioversion to restore sinus rhythm. His INR was subtherapeutic on admission, and he remained on warfarin and adjusted metoprolol dosing. He improved clinically but left against medical advice before formal discharge instructions could be completed. He was advised on weight monitoring, sodium and fluid restriction, medication adherence, and follow-up with cardiology and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
